are there any studies comparing kid outcomes in shared custody vs sole custody? like actual controlled studies not just opinion pieces

Yes, there is a substantial body of research on this. A 2018 meta-analysis by Linda Nielsen published in the Journal of Family Psychology reviewed 60 studies and found that children in shared physical custody had better outcomes across multiple measures—including academic performance, emotional health, behavioral problems, and quality of relationships with both parents—compared to children in sole custody arrangements. A Swedish longitudinal study by Bergström et al. also found lower stress levels in children with joint physical custody. Critics note selection effects, since cooperative parents are more likely to choose shared custody, but several studies attempted to control for parental conflict levels and still found benefits.

Kentucky did pass a rebuttable presumption of equal shared custody in 2018, making it one of the first states to do so. Early data is still limited, but preliminary reports suggest that the law has led to more shared custody arrangements and fewer contentious custody disputes, potentially because the presumption reduces the incentive for adversarial litigation. Proponents argue that states like Kentucky and Arizona, which have moved toward shared parenting defaults, are seeing lower relitigation rates. However, comprehensive longitudinal outcome data on child wellbeing under these new frameworks is still being collected, so definitive conclusions may take several more years.
